name: MEV-extractable ordering: sandwich, backrun, or JIT liquidity
requires: a swap or liquidity path whose price impact is visible in the mempool
no slippage bound, or a bound the attacker can sit inside
a pool with enough depth to move and enough volume to extract from
foundry with a fork RPC at the target block
questions: Does the swap pass minAmountOut / maxAmountIn, and is it derived from a live quote or a stale one?
Is the slippage tolerance wide enough that a sandwich of the observed depth still profits after fees?
Is the router callable by a contract that can front-run and back-run in one bundle?
Is there a deadline, and is it the block timestamp or a far-future constant?
Does the protocol itself rebalance on a schedule with no slippage bound?
Is a liquidation or oracle update callable in the same block as the price move it depends on?
For JIT: can liquidity be added before a swap and removed after within one block, keeping the fee?
What does the victim lose net of the attacker's gas and pool fee?
false_positives: Slippage is tight enough that the sandwich is unprofitable after fees
The swap is private / routed through a private mempool, so it cannot be front-run
Pool depth means the price impact needed costs more than the extractable amount
The protocol uses a TWAP the single-block move cannot shift
poc_must_show: a simulation of front-run + victim + back-run in one block with the attacker delta measured
a control run of the victim swap alone, same block, showing the difference
gas and pool fee deducted so the figure is net
the victim's loss stated alongside the attacker's gain
impact_bar: Reportable as a protocol-level MEV exposure when a generalised attacker profits net of fees at observed depth. Not reportable where the only cost bearer is the swapping user's own slippage setting.
